key_insight: Preserving recovered execution procedures in reusable artifacts raises mean ML reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6%.
engineering_relevance: Packaging code, environments, launchers, and reproduction guidance can make agent-driven experiment replication more reliable while lowering downstream API spending.
method: Use ReproBridge agents to construct refined reproducible artifacts.
Test raw code versus refined artifacts in fresh agent sessions.
Have a separate Auditor check execution evidence.
evidence_signal: Across four models on ReproBridge-Bench’s 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments and 36 papers, refined artifacts reduced downstream API spending by 19.7% on average and narrowed the success-rate spread from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points.
watch_item: The abstract does not report artifact-construction costs, so downstream API savings alone do not establish net cost savings.
paper_title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
